headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and write-conflict: Devin’s autonomous cloud workspace can feed unsafe outputs into social-auto-upload’s account actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can read files, browse, use MCP, and act autonomously in a shared integration environment; social-auto-upload consumes files and APIs for posting. That creates a plausible instruction-in-content bridge if Devin’s outputs are copied into upload inputs or account files. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is possible in default workflows.
conditions: IF Devin-generated text or files are pasted into social-auto-upload inputs without sanitization
IF social-auto-upload parses captions, metadata, or filenames as instructions
mitigations: Add a manual review step before any upload text is reused
Use a fixed template for captions and metadata
Strip markdown, code fences, and directives from imported text
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and secrets in a cloud workspace; social-auto-upload handles account data and media files. If the pair shares a workspace, repo, or account file path, sensitive content can flow from Devin into upload artifacts or logs. The profiles do not show isolation between these surfaces, so the safer assumption is a real leakage path.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same repo clone, cloud workspace, or account file directory
IF Devin writes secrets or internal docs into files later consumed by social-auto-upload
mitigations: Keep upload media in a separate directory from code and notes
Rotate any tokens that may have been copied into shared files
Review recent files for secrets before upload runs
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin has unrestricted cloud-workspace shell, filesystem write, and modify_git_state; social-auto-upload is CLI-based and may also mutate local account files or media outputs. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes can corrupt git state or overwrite files. Because the profiles do not document locking or coordination, uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository checkout or account file tree
IF either agent writes while the other is running without a lock
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time on shared paths
Use separate working directories for each agent
Commit or snapshot state before handing off between agents
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional workspace coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin can autonomously generate code, docs, and operational text; social-auto-upload can then act on files and account data. If B treats A’s generated captions, filenames, or instructions as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious output can cascade into incorrect uploads or account actions. The pair has no documented verification gate, so the downstream action risk is substantial.
conditions: IF social-auto-upload uses Devin-produced text as upload metadata or scheduling input
IF no human or validation step checks the generated content before posting
mitigations: Require human approval for every outbound post
Validate captions and targets against a whitelist
Compare generated metadata to source media before upload
requires-engineering: add schema validation and rejection rules

E_compliance.rationale: Devin handles team chat, issue trackers, docs, and secrets in a vendor-managed cloud workspace, while social-auto-upload touches account data and media. If regulated or internal data is moved from Devin into social posting workflows, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not show matching compliance controls, so the mismatch is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF internal docs, chat, or secrets from Devin are exported into social-auto-upload artifacts
IF the account data includes regulated or restricted content
mitigations: Classify data before transfer between agents
Exclude secrets and internal docs from upload inputs
Review retention settings for generated files and logs
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
